items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: one was with my brother Elvin and Richard Davis, the bass player

ctx.x: Hank Jones: I was over there for about two and a half weeks doing a promotional tour. I had done a couple of CDs; one was with my brother Elvin and Richard Davis, the bass player. They made – – I think they made two releases from that date. And I did another date with Jack DeJohnette and John Patitucci. But, these two albums were the objects of the promotion. I mean, they promote very, very heavily everyday. I must have had 40 interviews and about 30 record signings at the record shops, plus all of the recording.…
I've better not; it interferes with my talking.

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And he said, “Listen get your brushed and play along with me” So I got a chance to learn how to listen and play at the same time and control dynamics.

ctx.x: I can imagine that first day when you get that set home what was that like? What’d you do?

Fortunately you know Hank came home from time to time. And he would practice. And he said, “Listen get your brushed and play along with me” So I got a chance to learn how to listen and play at the same time and control dynamics. And hank he helped me do that.
Had you used brushes before that?
